title: Sequence-slice probes and conditional folding — grooming notes
content:
Purpose:
Capture a compact, actionable set of interaction patterns for two related improvements to the Trace Viewer UI that came up in grooming: 1) sequence-slice probes (a lightweight way to mark and jump to ordered span sequences) and 2) conditional folding rules for waterfalls (fold spans by pattern or condition rather than only by level).

Background / why now:
- Console users keep losing the hot path context when there are many background spans. We get repeated asks for better folding, ad-hoc slicing, and for making trace summaries reproducible between sessions.
- We have a small prototype that auto-clusters spans by attribution (service + operation). This doc explores UX primitives to expose that in an intuitive, keyboard-first workflow while keeping discoverability for new users.

Problem statement (short):
- Long traces with repeated noisy spans make it hard to locate the canonical sequence for a given request flow.
- Current fold/unfold model is manual and coarse (span-level + lane collapse). Users want: pattern-based folding, saved slice bookmarks, and quick comparisons between slices.

Design goals / constraints:
- Non-destructive: folding and slices are view-only and do not alter raw trace data.
- Fast discovery: keyboard + quick actions to capture or jump to a slice in <3s for power users.
- Shareable: slice + applied filters must be linkable and reproducible.
- Backwards-compatible: fall back to current collapse rules if feature toggles off.
- Accessible: should work with screen readers and without drag-only gestures.

High level proposals (3 complementary patterns):
1) Sequence-slice probes (lightweight bookmarks)
   - Interaction: user selects an anchor span, then shift+click additional spans (or command-click on mac) to form an ordered 'slice'. The slice appears as a thin overlay ribbon on the waterfall and in an ordered list in the right-side inspector.
   - UX affordances: transient highlight + micro-toolbar: [Save slice] [Compare] [Annotate] [Copy link]. If saved, becomes a named slice in the trace's left rail (under 'Slices').
   - Use cases: save hotpath for regression comparison across model versions, capture a replicated failure sequence to attach to ticket, quick-jump during incident.
   - Keyboard: start slice mode (S), navigate spans with j/k, add span (space), finish save (S again).

2) Conditional folding rules (pattern-based collapse)
   - Small rule language in the filter bar: examples: fold where service = "auth" AND duration < 10ms, or fold name ~ /redis|memcached/. UI builder exposes common presets: by-service, by-duration, by-tag, by-operation-regex.
   - Visual: folded regions compress into a single summary row with an expand caret and counts (e.g., "5x redis calls — 120ms total"). Hover shows a sparkline and sample span.
   - Toggle: preview mode shows folding applied locally; user can commit rule to a saved view. Rules can be combined with existing filters (time window, error-only).

3) Inline annotations + automatic sequence extraction
   - When a slice is saved, the viewer generates a compact text summary (auto-extracted: service chain, percent of total time, top N spans) and pins it to the top of the trace viewer.
   - The extractor runs heuristics (http->db->cache) but user can edit the summary. The annotation persists with the saved slice.

Wireframe notes (visuals described):
- Global layout unchanged: left rail (filters/slices), center waterfall, right inspector/context.
- Sequence-slice modal: small floating overlay near the waterfall when slice mode active. Contains ordered bullets of selected spans (operation — service — duration). Buttons: Save / Compare / Clear.
- Fold rule editor: in the filter bar a new pill "Fold rules" opens a popover with quick toggles (by service, by duration slider, regex input). A compact preview check toggle runs rules on the local trace for visual confirmation.

Interaction details / edge behaviours:
- Selecting spans for a slice across time: support selecting spans that aren't adjacent in the waterfall; when non-adjacent spans included, the slice label shows gaps (e.g., 1->3->6).
- Automatic collision handling: if saved slice name already exists, ask to overwrite or auto-append numeric suffix.
- Folded region expansion: clicking expand focuses and plays a small animation to avoid jarring layout jumps. When expanding a folded region that contains the active span, center on the active span.
- Persistence: saved slices and fold rules are saved to the trace view 'view state' (not global account prefs) and encoded in the shareable URL.

Accessibility & keyboard mapping:
- All actions have keyboard equivalents (S for slice mode, F for fold rule editor, Enter to apply rule).
- Folded summaries must surface readable text (e.g., "3x cache.calls — 45ms total") and be navigable by screen readers as a region with role=button to expand.

Metrics / acceptance criteria:
- Reduce median time-to-find-hotpath in user test from 45s -> 20s for traces >200 spans. (Follow-up usability test target)
- >60% of internal SRE participants prefer rule-based folding over manual collapse in the lab exercise.
- Saved slice link reproducibility: reproduced identical slices 95% of the time across two runs on same trace id (heuristics unit test).

Backlog grooming (explicit tickets to create / refine):
- TRACE-512: implement basic client-side slice selection UX (prototype only) — low risk
- TRACE-513: fold rule editor popover & preview engine (requires filter pipeline change) — medium
- TRACE-514: URL encoding for slices and fold rules + sharing semantics — high (needs backend support)
- TRACE-515: annotate-extractor service to auto-generate summaries (research: heuristics + ML fallback) — research spike
- TRACE-516: keyboard navigation polish + accessibility QA — small

Prototype links / assets:
- Figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/trace-slices-prototype (WIP)
- Quick capture demo: https://prod-console-scratch/redwood/demo/trace-slice.mp4 (internal)

Open questions / flags for eng:
- How expensive is it to run fold-rule preview on very large traces client-side? Need perf estimate from infra team. (Action: @Marco to sync with infra by 2025-11-12)
- What is the canonical storage for saved slices: per-trace, per-org, or per-user? Linkability implies per-trace storage; privacy concerns could push per-user.
- Should fold rules be part of saved 'view snapshots' that support rollouts in the console (e.g., default views for support teams)?

Decisions (temporary):
- MVP stores slices in the UI state and encodes them in the URL. Long-term persisted saves deferred to next quarter.
- Fold-rule language will be limited to simple comparisons + regex for MVP. Full boolean expression support deferred.

Notes to self / grooming leftovers:
- Need small microcopy for folded region summary — draft: "{count} calls — {sum_duration} total — {sample_op}"
- Validate map between span tags and rule editor dropdown (service / op name / attribute keys).
- Add unit tests for URL encoding size limits (slices + rules might hit query length).
- Schedule 30m cross-team review with SRE + Infra + DevEx next week.

Quick todo list (for next groom meeting):
- [ ] Confirm storage decision with security (Aisha)
- [ ] Get perf cost estimate for preview pipeline (Marco)
- [ ] Wireframe final micro-toolbar states (Elaine)
- [ ] Create TRACE tickets and estimate in next sprint (Samir)

Appendix — micro-interaction scripts (for prototyping)
- Slice keyboard flow: press S -> modal shows "slice mode" -> use j/k to navigate spans -> Space to add -> Escape to cancel -> Enter to save -> toast: "Slice saved — share link copied"
- Fold-rule quick flow: press F -> popover opens with top presets -> toggle preset -> preview animation runs -> press Apply -> toast: "View updated (temporary). Save to persist view."

End of doc.
